sanskrit: yatra gargeṇa vṛddhena tapasā bhāvitātmanā kālajñānagatiś caiva jyotiṣāṃ ca vyatikramaḥ
english: There it was that the aged Garga, his soul refined by austerity, attained the science of the reckoning of time and of the courses and transits of the heavenly bodies.

sanskrit: utpātā dāruṇāś caiva śubhāś ca janamejaya sarasvatyāḥ śubhe tīrthe vihitā vai mahātmanā tasya nāmnā ca tat tīrthaṃ gargasrota iti smṛtam
english: There too, O Janamejaya, the dread and the auspicious portents were determined by that great soul at the holy ford of the Sarasvatī; and after his name that ford is remembered as Gargasrotas.

sanskrit: tatra gargaṃ mahābhāgam ṛṣayaḥ suvratā nṛpa upāsāṃ cakrire nityaṃ kālajñānaṃ prati prabho
english: There, O king, the sages of firm vows constantly waited upon the illustrious Garga, O lord, to learn from him the science of time.

sanskrit: tatra gatvā mahārāja balaḥ śvetānulepanaḥ vidhivad dhi dhanaṃ dattvā munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām
english: Having gone there, O great king, Bala, anointed with white sandal paste, duly bestowed wealth upon the sages whose souls were refined.

sanskrit: uccāvacāṃs tathā bhakṣyān dvijebhyo vipradāya saḥ nīlavāsās tato 'gacchac chaṅkhatīrthaṃ mahāyaśāḥ
english: And having given to the brāhmaṇas foods of every kind, high and humble, that hero of great renown, clad in dark blue, then proceeded to the Śaṅkha ford.

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyan mahāśaṅkhaṃ mahāmerum ivocchritam śvetaparvatasaṃkāśam ṛṣisaṃghair niṣevitam sarasvatyās taṭe jātaṃ nagaṃ tāladhvajo balī
english: There the mighty Bala, the palmyra-bannered, beheld a great conch-tree, lofty as Mount Meru, resembling a white mountain, frequented by hosts of sages, a tree grown upon the bank of the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: yakṣā vidyādharāś caiva rākṣasāś cāmitaujasaḥ piśācāś cāmitabalā yatra siddhāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: There were yakṣas and vidyādharas and rākṣasas of boundless energy, and piśācas of measureless strength, and siddhas by the thousand.

sanskrit: te sarve hy aśanaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ tasya vanaspateḥ vrataiś ca niyamaiś caiva kāle kāle sma bhuñjate
english: All of them, forsaking other food, would from time to time eat only the fruit of that lord of the forest, observing their vows and restraints.

sanskrit: prāptaiś ca niyamais tais tair vicarantaḥ pṛthak pṛthak adṛśyamānā manujair vyacaran puruṣarṣabha
english: Keeping each his own appointed observances, they roamed about apart, one and all, and ranged there unseen by men, O bull among men.

sanskrit: evaṃ khyāto narapate loke 'smin sa vanaspatiḥ tatra tīrthaṃ sarasvatyāḥ pāvanaṃ lokaviśrutam
english: Thus famed in this world, O ruler of men, was that lord of the forest; and there upon the Sarasvatī is a purifying ford renowned throughout the world.

sanskrit: tasmiṃś ca yaduśārdūlo dattvā tīrthe yaśasvinām tāmrāyasāni bhāṇḍāni vastrāṇi vividhāni ca
english: At that ford the tiger of the Yadus bestowed upon the renowned sages vessels of copper and of iron and garments of every kind.

sanskrit: pūjayitvā dvijāṃś caiva pūjitaś ca tapodhanaiḥ puṇyaṃ dvaitavanaṃ rājann ājagāma halāyudhaḥ
english: Having honored the brāhmaṇas and being himself honored by those rich in austerity, Halāyudha came, O king, to the holy Dvaitavana.

sanskrit: tatra gatvā munīn dṛṣṭvā nānāveṣadharān balaḥ āplutya salile cāpi pūjayām āsa vai dvijān
english: Having gone there and beheld the sages wearing garbs of many kinds, Bala bathed in the water and paid honor to the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: tathaiva dattvā viprebhyaḥ paribhogān supuṣkalān tataḥ prāyād balo rājan dakṣiṇena sarasvatīm
english: And having likewise given the brāhmaṇas ample objects of enjoyment, Bala then set forth, O king, along the southern bank of the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: gatvā caiva mahābāhur nātidūraṃ mahāyaśāḥ dharmātmā nāgadhanvānaṃ tīrtham āgamad acyutaḥ
english: And that mighty-armed one of great renown, righteous of soul and unfailing, having gone no great distance, came to the ford named Nāgadhanvan.

sanskrit: yatra pannagarājasya vāsukeḥ saṃniveśanam mahādyuter mahārāja bahubhiḥ pannagair vṛtam yatrāsann ṛṣayaḥ siddhāḥ sahasrāṇi caturdaśa
english: There, O great king, was the abode of Vāsuki, king of serpents, of mighty splendor, surrounded by many serpents; and there dwelt fourteen thousand sages who had attained perfection.

sanskrit: yatra devāḥ samāgamya vāsukiṃ pannagottamam sarvapannagarājānam abhyaṣiñcan yathāvidhi pannagebhyo bhayaṃ tatra vidyate na sma kaurava
english: There the gods, having assembled, duly consecrated Vāsuki, foremost of serpents, as king over all the serpents; and there, O Kaurava, no fear of serpents is to be found.

sanskrit: tatrāpi vidhivad dattvā viprebhyo ratnasaṃcayān prāyāt prācīṃ diśaṃ rājan dīpyamānaḥ svatejasā
english: There too, having duly bestowed heaps of jewels upon the brāhmaṇas, he proceeded toward the east, O king, blazing with his own splendor.

sanskrit: āplutya bahuśo hṛṣṭas teṣu tīrtheṣu lāṅgalī dattvā vasu dvijātibhyo jagāmāti tapasvinaḥ
english: Bathing again and again with delight in those fords, the plough-bearer gave wealth to the twice-born and passed on, surpassingly given to austerity.

sanskrit: tatrasthān ṛṣisaṃghāṃs tān abhivādya halāyudhaḥ tato rāmo 'gamat tīrtham ṛṣibhiḥ sevitaṃ mahat
english: Having saluted the hosts of sages who abode there, Halāyudha—Rāma—then went to a great ford frequented by sages.

sanskrit: yatra bhūyo nivavṛte prāṅmukhā vai sarasvatī ṛṣīṇāṃ naimiṣeyāṇām avekṣārthaṃ mahātmanām
english: There the Sarasvatī once again turned back and flowed eastward, for the sake of the great-souled sages of the Naimiṣa forest.

sanskrit: nivṛttāṃ tāṃ saricchreṣṭhāṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā tu lāṅgalī babhūva vismito rājan balaḥ śvetānulepanaḥ
english: Beholding that best of rivers there turned back upon her course, Bala the plough-bearer, anointed with white sandal, was filled with wonder, O king.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kasmāt sarasvatī brahman nivṛttā prāṅmukhī tataḥ vyākhyātum etad icchāmi sarvam adhvaryusattama
english: Janamejaya said: Why, O brāhmaṇa, did the Sarasvatī turn back and flow eastward? I wish to hear all this explained, O best of priests.

sanskrit: kasmiṃś ca kāraṇe tatra vismito yadunandanaḥ vinivṛttā saricchreṣṭhā katham etad dvijottama
english: And for what cause was the joy of the Yadus filled with wonder there, and how did that best of rivers turn back? Tell me this, O most excellent of the twice-born.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pūrvaṃ kṛtayuge rājan naimiṣeyās tapasvinaḥ vartamāne subahule satre dvādaśavārṣike ṛṣayo bahavo rājaṃs tatra saṃpratipedire
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Of old, in the Kṛta age, O king, the ascetics of the Naimiṣa forest were holding a vast sacrificial session lasting twelve years; and many sages, O king, assembled there together.

sanskrit: uṣitvā ca mahābhāgās tasmin satre yathāvidhi nivṛtte naimiṣeye vai satre dvādaśavārṣike ājagmur ṛṣayas tatra bahavas tīrthakāraṇāt
english: And when those illustrious ones had dwelt at that session according to the ordinance, and the twelve-year session of the Naimiṣa sages had come to its close, many sages came thither for the sake of the holy fords.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇāṃ bahulatvāt tu sarasvatyā viśāṃ pate tīrthāni nagarāyante kūle vai dakṣiṇe tadā
english: And by reason of the multitude of sages, O lord of peoples, the fords along the southern bank of the Sarasvatī then took on the likeness of cities.

sanskrit: samantapañcakaṃ yāvat tāvat te dvijasattamāḥ tīrthalobhān naravyāghra nadyās tīraṃ samāśritāḥ
english: As far as Samantapañcaka, O tiger among men, those most excellent of the twice-born, longing for the holy fords, took their stand along the river's shore.

sanskrit: juhvatāṃ tatra teṣāṃ tu munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām svādhyāyenāpi mahatā babhūvuḥ pūritā diśaḥ
english: As those sages of refined souls offered their oblations, the quarters of the sky were filled with the mighty sound of their study of the sacred texts.

sanskrit: agnihotrais tatas teṣāṃ hūyamānair mahātmanām aśobhata saricchreṣṭhā dīpyamānaiḥ samantataḥ
english: Then, with the fire-oblations of those great souls being offered and blazing on every side, the best of rivers shone resplendent.

sanskrit: vālakhilyā mahārāja aśmakuṭṭāś ca tāpasāḥ dantolūkhalinaś cānye saṃprakṣālās tathāpare
english: There were the Vālakhilyas, O great king, and ascetics who ground their food with stones, and others who used their teeth for a mortar, and still others who washed clean all they ate.

sanskrit: vāyubhakṣā jalāhārāḥ parṇabhakṣāś ca tāpasāḥ nānāniyamayuktāś ca tathā sthaṇḍilaśāyinaḥ
english: And ascetics who fed on air, who took only water, who ate but leaves, who kept observances of many kinds, and who lay upon the bare ground.

sanskrit: āsan vai munayas tatra sarasvatyāḥ samīpataḥ śobhayantaḥ saricchreṣṭhāṃ gaṅgām iva divaukasaḥ
english: Such sages dwelt there beside the Sarasvatī, gracing that best of rivers as the dwellers of heaven grace the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: tataḥ paścāt samāpetur ṛṣayaḥ satrayājinaḥ te 'vakāśaṃ na dadṛśuḥ kurukṣetre mahāvratāḥ
english: Thereafter came other sages, performers of sacrificial sessions; but those keepers of mighty vows found no open room for them in Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit: tato yajñopavītais te tat tīrthaṃ nirmimāya vai juhuvuś cāgnihotrāṇi cakruś ca vividhāḥ kriyāḥ
english: Then with their sacred threads they measured out a ford for themselves, offered their fire-oblations, and performed rites of many kinds.

sanskrit: tatas tam ṛṣisaṃghātaṃ nirāśaṃ cintayānvitam darśayām āsa rājendra teṣām arthe sarasvatī
english: Then, O lord of kings, the Sarasvatī showed herself for their sake to that company of sages who were dejected and sunk in anxious thought.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuñjān bahūn kṛtvā saṃnivṛttā saridvarā ṛṣīṇāṃ puṇyatapasāṃ kāruṇyāj janamejaya
english: Then, out of compassion for the sages of holy austerities, the best of rivers turned back her course, forming many bowers, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: tato nivṛtya rājendra teṣām arthe sarasvatī bhūyaḥ pratīcyabhimukhī susrāva saritāṃ varā
english: Then, having turned back for their sake, O lord of kings, the Sarasvatī, best of rivers, flowed once more toward the west.

sanskrit: amoghā gamanaṃ kṛtvā teṣāṃ bhūyo vrajāmy aham ity adbhutaṃ mahac cakre tato rājan mahānadī
english: "Not in vain shall my coming be: for their sake I flow back again,"—and so, O king, the great river wrought a great marvel.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa kuñjo rājendra naimiṣeya iti smṛtaḥ kurukṣetre kuruśreṣṭha kuruṣva mahatīḥ kriyāḥ
english: Thus, O lord of kings, that bower in Kurukṣetra is remembered as Naimiṣeya; there, O best of the Kurus, perform great rites.

sanskrit: tatra kuñjān bahūn dṛṣṭvā saṃnivṛttāṃ ca tāṃ nadīm babhūva vismayas tatra rāmasyātha mahātmanaḥ
english: Beholding there the many bowers and that river turned back upon her course, wonder then came over the great-souled Rāma.

sanskrit: upaspṛśya tu tatrāpi vidhivad yadunandanaḥ dattvā dāyān dvijātibhyo bhāṇḍāni vividhāni ca bhakṣyaṃ peyaṃ ca vividhaṃ brāhmaṇān pratyapādayat
english: There too the joy of the Yadus touched the water according to the rite, and bestowed gifts upon the twice-born—vessels of many kinds and food and drink of every sort he supplied to the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāyād balo rājan pūjyamāno dvijātibhiḥ sarasvatītīrthavaraṃ nānādvijagaṇāyutam
english: Then Bala set forth, O king, honored by the twice-born, to an excellent ford of the Sarasvatī thronged with hosts of birds of many kinds.

sanskrit: badareṅgudakāśmaryaplakṣāśvatthavibhītakaiḥ panasaiś ca palāśaiś ca karīraiḥ pīlubhis tathā
english: It was adorned with jujube and iṅguda, kāśmarya and plakṣa, fig-tree and vibhītaka, with breadfruit and palāśa, with karīra and pīlu trees.

sanskrit: sarasvatītīraruhair bandhanaiḥ syandanais tathā parūṣakavanaiś caiva bilvair āmrātakais tathā
english: And with trees grown on the Sarasvatī's bank—the bandhana and the syandana, with groves of parūṣaka, and with bilva and āmrātaka trees.

sanskrit: atimuktakaṣaṇḍaiś ca pārijātaiś ca śobhitam kadalīvanabhūyiṣṭham iṣṭaṃ kāntaṃ manoramam
english: It was graced with thickets of atimuktaka and with pārijāta trees, abounding most in groves of plantain—a place beloved, lovely, and delightful to the heart.

sanskrit: vāyvambuphalaparṇādair dantolūkhalikair api tathāśmakuṭṭair vāneyair munibhir bahubhir vṛtam
english: It was peopled by many forest sages who fed on air, on water, on fruit, and on leaves, who used their teeth for a mortar, and who ground their food with stones.

sanskrit: svādhyāyaghoṣasaṃghuṣṭaṃ mṛgayūthaśatākulam ahiṃsrair dharmaparamair nṛbhir atyantasevitam
english: It resounded with the chant of sacred study, was thronged with hundreds of herds of deer, and was much frequented by men who did no harm and held righteousness supreme.

sanskrit: saptasārasvataṃ tīrtham ājagāma halāyudhaḥ yatra maṅkaṇakaḥ siddhas tapas tepe mahāmuniḥ
english: To the ford named Saptasārasvata Halāyudha came, where the great sage Maṅkaṇaka, who had won perfection, had performed his austerities.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca saptasārasvataṃ kasmāt kaś ca maṅkaṇako muniḥ kathaṃ siddhaś ca bhagavān kaś cāsya niyamo 'bhavat
english: Janamejaya said: Why is it called Saptasārasvata, and who was the sage Maṅkaṇaka? How did the venerable one win perfection, and what was the observance he kept?

sanskrit: kasya vaṃśe samutpannaḥ kiṃ cādhītaṃ dvijottama etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ vidhivad dvijasattama
english: In whose lineage was he born, and what did he learn, O most excellent of the twice-born? All this I wish to hear in due order, O best of brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca rājan sapta sarasvatyo yābhir vyāptam idaṃ jagat āhūtā balavadbhir hi tatra tatra sarasvatī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: O king, there are seven Sarasvatīs, by whom this world is pervaded; for, summoned by the mighty here and there, the Sarasvatī came.

sanskrit: suprabhā kāñcanākṣī ca viśālā mānasahradā sarasvatī oghavatī suveṇur vimalodakā
english: They are Suprabhā and Kāñcanākṣī, Viśālā and Mānasahradā, the Sarasvatī known as Oghavatī, Suveṇu, and Vimalodakā.

sanskrit: pitāmahasya mahato vartamāne mahītale vitate yajñavāṭe vai sameteṣu dvijātiṣu
english: While a sacrifice of the mighty Grandsire was in progress upon the earth, the sacrificial enclosure spread wide and the twice-born assembled there—

sanskrit: puṇyāhaghoṣair vimalair vedānāṃ ninadais tathā deveṣu caiva vyagreṣu tasmin yajñavidhau tadā
english: with the pure proclamations of the holy day and the resounding of the Vedas, while the gods themselves were intent upon that sacrificial rite—

sanskrit: tatra caiva mahārāja dīkṣite prapitāmahe yajatas tatra satreṇa sarvakāmasamṛddhinā
english: there, O great king, when the great-grandsire had been consecrated and was offering a session that fulfilled every desire,

sanskrit: manasā cintitā hy arthā dharmārthakuśalais tadā upatiṣṭhanti rājendra dvijātīṃs tatra tatra ha
english: whatever things the twice-born, skilled in righteousness and worldly gain, conceived in their minds, those things, O lord of kings, came to them there of their own accord.

sanskrit: jaguś ca tatra gandharvā nanṛtuś cāpsarogaṇāḥ vāditrāṇi ca divyāni vādayām āsur añjasā
english: There the gandharvas sang, and the troops of apsarases danced, and divine instruments of music were straightway sounded.

sanskrit: tasya yajñasya saṃpattyā tutuṣur devatā api vismayaṃ paramaṃ jagmuḥ kim u mānuṣayonayaḥ
english: At the perfection of that sacrifice even the gods were delighted and fell into the utmost wonder—how much more, then, those of mortal birth?

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā yajñe puṣkarasthe pitāmahe abruvann ṛṣayo rājan nāyaṃ yajño mahāphalaḥ na dṛśyate saricchreṣṭhā yasmād iha sarasvatī
english: As the sacrifice went forward thus, with the Grandsire abiding at Puṣkara, the sages said, O king: "This sacrifice cannot bear great fruit, since the best of rivers, the Sarasvatī, is nowhere seen here."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā bhagavān prītaḥ sasmārātha sarasvatīm pitāmahena yajatā āhūtā puṣkareṣu vai suprabhā nāma rājendra nāmnā tatra sarasvatī
english: Hearing this, the venerable one was pleased and called the Sarasvatī to mind; and being summoned by the sacrificing Grandsire, the Sarasvatī came to Puṣkara, there bearing the name Suprabhā, O lord of kings.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā munayas tuṣṭā vegayuktāṃ sarasvatīm pitāmahaṃ mānayantīṃ kratuṃ te bahu menire
english: Beholding the swift-flowing Sarasvatī, who came to do honor to the Grandsire, the sages were gladdened and held that sacrifice in high esteem.

sanskrit: evam eṣā saricchreṣṭhā puṣkareṣu sarasvatī pitāmahārthaṃ saṃbhūtā tuṣṭyarthaṃ ca manīṣiṇām
english: Thus this best of rivers, the Sarasvatī, came into being at Puṣkara for the Grandsire's sake and for the delight of the wise.

sanskrit: naimiṣe munayo rājan samāgamya samāsate tatra citrāḥ kathā hy āsan vedaṃ prati janeśvara
english: At the Naimiṣa forest, O king, the sages assembled and sat together; and there, O lord of peoples, wondrous discourses arose concerning the Veda.

sanskrit: tatra te munayo hy āsan nānāsvādhyāyavedinaḥ te samāgamya munayaḥ sasmarur vai sarasvatīm
english: There were sages versed in the recitation of various branches of sacred lore; and those sages, having gathered, called the Sarasvatī to mind.

sanskrit: sā tu dhyātā mahārāja ṛṣibhiḥ satrayājibhiḥ samāgatānāṃ rājendra sahāyārthaṃ mahātmanām ājagāma mahābhāgā tatra puṇyā sarasvatī
english: Thus meditated upon, O great king, by the sages who were performing the session, the illustrious and holy Sarasvatī came thither, O lord of kings, to aid those great souls who had assembled.

sanskrit: naimiṣe kāñcanākṣī tu munīnāṃ satrayājinām āgatā saritāṃ śreṣṭhā tatra bhārata pūjitā
english: At the Naimiṣa forest the best of rivers came as Kāñcanākṣī, and there, O Bhārata, she was worshipped by the sages who performed the session.

sanskrit: gayasya yajamānasya gayeṣv eva mahākratum āhūtā saritāṃ śreṣṭhā gayayajñe sarasvatī
english: When Gaya was offering a great sacrifice at Gayā, the best of rivers, the Sarasvatī, was summoned to the sacrifice of Gaya.

sanskrit: viśālāṃ tu gayeṣv āhur ṛṣayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ sarit sā himavatpārśvāt prasūtā śīghragāminī
english: At Gayā the sages of strict vows call her Viśālā—that swift-flowing river, born from the side of Himavat.

sanskrit: auddālakes tathā yajñe yajatas tatra bhārata samete sarvataḥ sphīte munīnāṃ maṇḍale tadā
english: And at the sacrifice of Auddālaka, when he was offering it, O Bhārata, with a great circle of sages assembled there from every side,

sanskrit: uttare kosalābhāge puṇye rājan mahātmanaḥ auddālakena yajatā pūrvaṃ dhyātā sarasvatī
english: in the northern region of Kosala, O king, the holy place of that great soul, the Sarasvatī was first called to mind by the sacrificing Auddālaka.

sanskrit: ājagāma saricchreṣṭhā taṃ deśam ṛṣikāraṇāt pūjyamānā munigaṇair valkalājinasaṃvṛtaiḥ manohradeti vikhyātā sā hi tair manasā hṛtā
english: The best of rivers came to that country for the sages' sake, honored by hosts of sages clad in bark and deerskin; and because she was drawn thither by their minds, she became famed as Mānasahradā.

sanskrit: suveṇur ṛṣabhadvīpe puṇye rājarṣisevite kuroś ca yajamānasya kurukṣetre mahātmanaḥ ājagāma mahābhāgā saricchreṣṭhā sarasvatī
english: As Suveṇu the illustrious best of rivers, the Sarasvatī, came to the holy isle of Ṛṣabha, frequented by royal sages, and to Kurukṣetra when the great-souled Kuru was sacrificing there.

sanskrit: oghavaty api rājendra vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā samāhūtā kurukṣetre divyatoyā sarasvatī
english: As Oghavatī too, O lord of kings, the Sarasvatī of divine waters was summoned at Kurukṣetra by the great soul Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: dakṣeṇa yajatā cāpi gaṅgādvāre sarasvatī vimalodā bhagavatī brahmaṇā yajatā punaḥ samāhūtā yayau tatra puṇye haimavate girau
english: And summoned by Dakṣa when he sacrificed at Gaṅgādvāra, the divine Sarasvatī came as Vimalodā; and again, summoned by Brahmā at his sacrifice, she went thither to the holy mountain of Himavat.

sanskrit: ekībhūtās tatas tās tu tasmiṃs tīrthe samāgatāḥ saptasārasvataṃ tīrthaṃ tatas tat prathitaṃ bhuvi
english: Then those seven, gathered together at that ford, became one; and thus that ford became renowned upon the earth as Saptasārasvata.

sanskrit: iti sapta sarasvatyo nāmataḥ parikīrtitāḥ saptasārasvataṃ caiva tīrthaṃ puṇyaṃ tathā smṛtam
english: Thus the seven Sarasvatīs have been proclaimed by name, and thus too the holy ford of Saptasārasvata is remembered.

sanskrit: śṛṇu maṅkaṇakasyāpi kaumārabrahmacāriṇaḥ āpagām avagāḍhasya rājan prakrīḍitaṃ mahat
english: Hear now of the great sport of Maṅkaṇaka also, who had kept the vow of celibacy from his boyhood, when he had plunged into the river, O king.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā yadṛcchayā tatra striyam ambhasi bhārata snāyantīṃ rucirāpāṅgīṃ digvāsasam aninditām sarasvatyāṃ mahārāja caskande vīryam ambhasi
english: Beholding by chance there in the water, O Bhārata, a woman bathing—fair of glance, clad only in the quarters of the sky, and blameless—his seed, O great king, fell into the waters of the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: tad retaḥ sa tu jagrāha kalaśe vai mahātapāḥ saptadhā pravibhāgaṃ tu kalaśasthaṃ jagāma ha tatrarṣayaḥ sapta jātā jajñire marutāṃ gaṇāḥ
english: That seed the great ascetic gathered into a jar; and there within the jar it split into seven parts, and from it were born seven sages, the hosts of the Maruts.
